title.narrative: Voices in Motion: Youth Arts & Rights

description.narrative:
Voices in Motion is a 12-month transnational, youth-led project in Italy and Kenya (Rivalta di Torino and Nairobi) that strengthensyoung people’s participation in decision-making on comprehensive sexuality education (CSE), sexual and reproductive healthand rights (SRHR), gender-based violence prevention, access to health services, and LGBTQIA+ rights. The project uses arts and culture—music,performance, storytelling, and digital media—as accessible advocacy tools to foster dialogue between youth, localcommunities, and decision-makers. It directly involves at least 30 young people aged 18–35, prioritising those facing social, economic, cultural, or access-related barriers. Through capacity building, participatory research, artistic co-creation, and public cultural events in both countries, participants become advocates and facilitators. The process culminates in a joint policy brief with actionable recommendations and follow-up commitments to sustain engagement beyond the project.
The main goal of the project is to strengthen young people’s capacity to advocate on sexuality, health and rights, gender-based violence prevention, access to youth-friendly health services, and LGBTQIA+ rights, while fostering sustained dialogue between youth, communities,and decision-makers through artistic and cultural advocacy initiatives.
Expected changes within 12 months: - Direct involvement of at least 30 young people, with ≥50% facing fewer opportunities - Measurable increase in skills and confidence throughtraining and ongoing support - Activation of 10 youth leaders as facilitators and spokespersons - Participatory research: 40 interviews and 2 focus groups to map barriers and solutions - Creative labs and public cultural events in both countries as spaces for dialogue and exchange
Realistic policy/dialogue results: - Dialogue moments with the Departments/Assessorati for Youth Policies and International Cooperation in both territories - A joint Policy Brief with ≥5 actionable recommendations plusdocumented follow-up commitments
Expected impacts include: - Increased confidence, skills, and leadership among participating youth to engage in advocacy and dialogue - Greater recognition of youth-led artistic initiatives as valid advocacy spaces by local stakeholders - Improved communication and trust between young people and decision-makers - Continued collaboration and follow-up actions beyond the project timeframe

participating-org.narrative:
In(t)essere APS is a youth-led non-profit organisation based in Rivalta di Torino, in the metropolitan area of Turin (Italy). The organisation works to promote youth empowerment, social inclusion, and active citizenship, with a specific focus on young people facing social, economic, or cultural barriers.
The vision of In(t)essere APS is to contribute to a more inclusive and participatory society, where young people are aware of their potential and recognised as active actors in their communities. The organisation believes in youth participation as a driver for social change and democratic life.
Its mission is to design and implement educational, cultural, and community-based projects that strengthen young people’s personal, social, and civic competences. In(t)essere APS adopts non-formal education methodologies and uses artistic and cultural practices—such as theatre, music, and participatory cultural production—as tools for expression, dialogue, and empowerment.
The organisation’s main objectives include fostering youth-led initiatives, supporting young people with fewer opportunities, promoting inclusion and diversity, and strengthening links between young people,local communities, and institutions.
The core values of In(t)essere APS are equality, inclusiveness, participation, anti-discrimination, and solidarity. The organisation is committed to creating safe and accessible spaces where young people can experiment, learnby doing, and actively contribute to the cultural and social life of their territories.
